question: How can time-resolved photoluminescence techniques improve imaging contrast and sensing sensitivity in bioimaging and biosensing?
answer: Time-resolved photoluminescence techniques enhance imaging contrast and sensing sensitivity in bioimaging and biosensing by selectively detecting long-lived luminescent signals while suppressing short-lived autofluorescence and background noise. Time-gated luminescence (TGL) applies a delay between excitation and detection to isolate probe signals, improving accuracy, while photoluminescence lifetime imaging (PLIM) distinguishes probes based on their unique decay lifetimes for higher time-domain resolution. These techniques are particularly effective with long-lived probes such as lanthanides, transition-metal complexes, and persistent phosphors, which exhibit tunable emission properties and prolonged lifetimes. Additionally, combining time-resolved methods with near-infrared (NIR) excitation further improves tissue penetration depth and reduces phototoxicity. Future advancements focus on developing biocompatible probes, optimizing lifetime responses to analytes, and integrating time-resolved detection with advanced imaging modalities for higher precision and sensitivity.
